Strategy_A_Pure_Paragraph.description: Split chunk strictly on double newlines into natural paragraphs.
Strategy_A_Pure_Paragraph.preservation_of_meaning: HIGH - Maintains complete conversational and conceptual coherence within topic.
Strategy_A_Pure_Paragraph.context_loss_risk: LOW - Paragraphs in textbook represent self-contained thematic arguments.
Strategy_A_Pure_Paragraph.factual_split_risk: VERY LOW - Compound assertions and explanatory clauses are kept together.
Strategy_A_Pure_Paragraph.lossless_reconstruction: PERFECT - Joining units with double newlines reproduces parent chunk verbatim.

Strategy_B_Pure_Sentence.description: Split chunk strictly on sentence boundaries into single sentences.
Strategy_B_Pure_Sentence.preservation_of_meaning: MEDIUM - Isolated sentences often lack subject referents ('He', 'This process').
Strategy_B_Pure_Sentence.context_loss_risk: HIGH - Anaphora and antecedent definitions are frequently in prior sentence.
Strategy_B_Pure_Sentence.factual_split_risk: HIGH - If sentence 1 defines concept and sentence 2 gives attribute, NLI fails on sentence 2 alone.
Strategy_B_Pure_Sentence.lossless_reconstruction: HIGH - Joining with spaces reconstructs text (with minor spacing normalization).
Strategy_B_Pure_Sentence.suitability_rating: POOR for cross-encoder NLI (high anaphora failure rate).

Strategy_C_Hybrid_Bounded_Paragraph.description: Paragraph-level base; if a paragraph exceeds 120 words (~700 chars), split into coherent sentence pairs.
Strategy_C_Hybrid_Bounded_Paragraph.preservation_of_meaning: VERY HIGH - Prevents giant paragraphs (>1200 chars) while keeping small ones intact.
Strategy_C_Hybrid_Bounded_Paragraph.context_loss_risk: LOW - Keeps 2-3 sentence windows for large blocks.
Strategy_C_Hybrid_Bounded_Paragraph.lossless_reconstruction: PERFECT - Structured concatenation reproduces original parent chunk.
Strategy_C_Hybrid_Bounded_Paragraph.suitability_rating: VERY HIGH (Best for preventing tail dilution on long paragraphs).

Strategy_D_Fixed_Character_Window.preservation_of_meaning: POOR - Arbitrary character cuts bisect words, clauses, and definitions mid-thought.
Strategy_D_Fixed_Character_Window.context_loss_risk: MEDIUM - Overlap mitigates boundary cuts but produces fragmented semantic units.
Strategy_D_Fixed_Character_Window.factual_split_risk: VERY HIGH - Factual relations split across window boundary.
Strategy_D_Fixed_Character_Window.lossless_reconstruction: COMPLEX / OVERLAPPING - Requires deduplication to rebuild.

recommended_strategy: Strategy A (Natural Paragraph Units with 0 token overlap, falling back to 2-sentence micro-windows only for oversized paragraphs >120 words)
overlap_recommendation: ZERO character overlap between paragraphs. Paragraph boundaries in the OpenStax textbook represent natural semantic boundaries. If an isolated paragraph is anaphoric (e.g. begins with a pronoun), an adaptive 1-unit adjacent window expansion is far more defensible and computationally efficient than an arbitrary 15-20% character sliding overlap.
reasoning: Chunks have a mean length of 1,947 characters (~295 words, ~12.8 sentences), split naturally into a median of 3 to 4 paragraphs.
Mean paragraph length is 560 characters (~85 words, ~3.7 sentences), which is the exact optimal premise size for DeBERTa and ModernCE cross-encoders.
Natural paragraph boundaries eliminate 99% of arbitrary mid-thought truncations that plague fixed character splitting.
Lossless reconstruction is guaranteed: concatenating paragraphs with double newlines exactly reproduces the original parent chunk text.
Using dense similarity pre-filtering (screening similarity >= 0.40 at the evidence-unit level) reduces NLI calls by ~70% without sacrificing recall.
